    Plotting a NetCDF¶

    NetCDF.plot plots a 2-D slice of a NetCDF variable through the same cleopatra path as Dataset.plot, but its surface is shaped around variables and dimensions: you name the variable, pin the slice with a Selectors bag, lay out panels with a FacetSpec, and share the colour vocabulary. This gallery shows each, plus animation over a dimension and the backend= seam.

    Setup¶

    Inline figures, imports, and the notebook-relative data path.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    %matplotlib inline
from pathlib import Path

from pyramids.netcdf import FacetSpec, NetCDF, Selectors
from pyramids.plot import ColorBar, ColorScaling

DATA = Path('../../../examples/data')
    %matplotlib inline from pathlib import Path from pyramids.netcdf import FacetSpec, NetCDF, Selectors from pyramids.plot import ColorBar, ColorScaling DATA = Path('../../../examples/data')

    Load a small CF file with one variable, values, over a 3-step band dimension named bands (coordinate values [5, 6, 7]) on a 13x14 grid.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    nc = NetCDF.read_file(str(DATA / 'netcdf' / 'cf__4v__1d3-3d1__proj__y-desc.nc'))
nc.variable_names
    nc = NetCDF.read_file(str(DATA / 'netcdf' / 'cf__4v__1d3-3d1__proj__y-desc.nc')) nc.variable_names

    Quickstart¶

    Name the variable; with no selector plot renders the first slice along the band dimension, with no-data masked.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    nc.plot(variable='values')
    nc.plot(variable='values')
    /home/runner/work/pyramids-core/pyramids-core/.pixi/envs/docs/lib/python3.14/site-packages/matplotlib/colors.py:824: RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in multiply
  xa *= self.N
    Out[3]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.array_glyph.ArrayGlyph at 0x7f6eb83eaf90>

    Selecting a slice: selectors=¶

    Selectors pins which 2-D slice to draw. Use isel for a positional index along a dimension, or sel for a coordinate value.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    nc.plot(variable='values', selectors=Selectors(isel={'bands': 0}))
    nc.plot(variable='values', selectors=Selectors(isel={'bands': 0}))
    /home/runner/work/pyramids-core/pyramids-core/.pixi/envs/docs/lib/python3.14/site-packages/matplotlib/colors.py:824: RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in multiply
  xa *= self.N
    Out[4]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.array_glyph.ArrayGlyph at 0x7f6eb781f890>
    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    nc.plot(variable='values', selectors=Selectors(sel={'bands': 6.0}))
    nc.plot(variable='values', selectors=Selectors(sel={'bands': 6.0}))

    The renderer: kind=¶

    The same renderer choices as Dataset.plot.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    nc.plot(variable='values', kind='contourf')
    nc.plot(variable='values', kind='contourf')
    Out[6]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.array_glyph.ArrayGlyph at 0x7f6f347db610>

    Colour: colorbar= and color=¶

    The grouped colour vocabulary is shared with the raster path — a labelled ColorBar and a typed ColorScaling norm.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    nc.plot(
    variable='values',
    colorbar=ColorBar(label='value', orientation='horizontal'),
    color=ColorScaling.power(gamma=0.7),
)
    nc.plot( variable='values', colorbar=ColorBar(label='value', orientation='horizontal'), color=ColorScaling.power(gamma=0.7), )
    /home/runner/work/pyramids-core/pyramids-core/.pixi/envs/docs/lib/python3.14/site-packages/matplotlib/colors.py:824: RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in multiply
  xa *= self.N

    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.array_glyph.ArrayGlyph at 0x7f6eb76e9e50>

    Faceting: facet=¶

    FacetSpec lays the slices along a dimension out as a panel grid — one panel per band here. The return becomes a cleopatra FacetGrid.

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    nc.plot(variable='values', facet=FacetSpec(col='bands'))
    nc.plot(variable='values', facet=FacetSpec(col='bands'))
    Out[8]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.array_glyph.FacetGrid at 0x7f6eb7546f90>
    /home/runner/work/pyramids-core/pyramids-core/.pixi/envs/docs/lib/python3.14/site-packages/matplotlib/colors.py:824: RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in multiply
  xa *= self.N

    Basemap: basemap=¶

    As for a raster, basemap=True adds a web-tile backdrop beneath the slice.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    nc.plot(variable='values', basemap=True)
    nc.plot(variable='values', basemap=True)
    /home/runner/work/pyramids-core/pyramids-core/.pixi/envs/docs/lib/python3.14/site-packages/matplotlib/colors.py:824: RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in multiply
  xa *= self.N
    Out[9]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.array_glyph.ArrayGlyph at 0x7f6eb728ce10>

    Animation: animate=¶

    Pass animate=<dim> (or animate=True) to sweep the slices along a dimension into an animation. plot returns a glyph whose anim is a matplotlib FuncAnimation.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    from IPython.display import HTML

glyph = nc.plot(variable='values', animate='bands')
HTML(glyph.anim.to_jshtml())
    from IPython.display import HTML glyph = nc.plot(variable='values', animate='bands') HTML(glyph.anim.to_jshtml())
    Out[10]:

    Choosing a renderer with backend=¶

    Every plot and animate method takes a keyword-only backend=. The default, "matplotlib", draws through cleopatra — that is every figure above. Any other name is resolved at call time through the pyramids.plot_backends entry-point group, with an optional fall-back to digitalearth's richer tiers. pyramids declares no dependency on any non-matplotlib renderer, so a bare install always plots through matplotlib.

    backend= Renderer Install
    "matplotlib" (default) cleopatra / matplotlib — static figures included with the [viz] extra
    "interactive" digitalearth (HoloViz / Bokeh) pip install 'digitalearth[interactive]'
    "3d" digitalearth (PyVista) pip install 'digitalearth[3d]'
    "web" digitalearth (MapLibre / deck.gl) pip install 'digitalearth[web]'

    Stating the default explicitly produces exactly the quickstart figure; the digitalearth tiers follow:

    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    nc.plot(variable='values', backend='matplotlib')
    nc.plot(variable='values', backend='matplotlib')
    /home/runner/work/pyramids-core/pyramids-core/.pixi/envs/docs/lib/python3.14/site-packages/matplotlib/colors.py:824: RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in multiply
  xa *= self.N
    Out[11]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.array_glyph.ArrayGlyph at 0x7f6eb4fba0d0>

    The digitalearth tiers today¶

    digitalearth's interactive / 3d / web renderers draw raster inputs. A NetCDF is a multi-variable cube whose variable must be selected first, which digitalearth 0.13 does not yet accept through quickmap, so those backends are not shown here — see the Dataset gallery for live interactive, web and 3-D output on a raster. Wiring NetCDF support into digitalearth is upstream work in the digitalearth repo; until it lands, NetCDF.plot renders through matplotlib (every figure above). The backend= seam itself is ready — it already resolves and dispatches to digitalearth the moment digitalearth supports the input type.

    Takeaway¶

    NetCDF.plot keeps the raster colour vocabulary while adding variable selection, Selectors slicing, FacetSpec panel grids and dimension animation — and backend= routes the whole lot to a richer renderer when one is installed.
